clue.text: Forlorn dig at restructuring in bank area

indicators.note: restructuring says the letters of the three words before it are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy report about a bank's reorganisation of one of its departments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restructuring' rearranges FORLORN, DIG and AT into the twelve letters of both linked lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading floor is the area of a bank or exchange where dealers buy and sell securities.

clue.text: Die long time after the Hardy girl

indicators.note: after places the long period behind the girl's name in the answer

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A girl from a Hardy novel dies after a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' looks like a verb but is the noun: a small cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small cube of stone or glass, as used in mosaic or as a die in antiquity.

clue.text: Defender god denied one of two students essential meaning

indicators.note: denied says the god's name has a piece taken away from it

parts.note: Apollo is the Greek god of the sun and music
L is the learner, student, abbreviation; the god's name has two of them and loses one
the gist is the essential meaning of something

explanation.surface: A god's defender rejects a student's interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is someone who argues in defence of a doctrine or cause.

clue.text: Some mountain troops opening passage

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alpine soldiers make their way through an opening pass.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or writing, a short form of introduction.

clue.text: Writer with books seen in expensive bar

parts.note: William Golding wrote Lord of the Flies
OT, Old Testament, is a common abbreviation for a set of books

explanation.surface: An author with his books is spotted in a pricey pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a block of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold ingot is a cast bar of precious metal, about as costly as bars come.

clue.text: See 9
Looking for a great deal

definitions.meaning: 'a ...' is an informal phrase for a lot, as in 'a ... better'

explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the act of seeing, and 'a sight more' colloquially means a great deal more.

clue.text: See less reason to trust of late his creation

indicators.note: creation says the letters of the preceding words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A recent work by a writer has made people doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose faith is to stop believing or trusting, finding less reason to rely on someone.

clue.text: Old school one for regression and subconscious view

indicators.note: for regression says the whole string of pieces is read going backwards

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traditional psychoanalyst uses regression to probe the subconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for regression' turns OGAMI round. 'Old school' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology an imago is an idealised mental image of a person held in the unconscious.

clue.text: Happiness all around for Ron dancing in Clare's town

indicators.note: all around says the happiness word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: glee means joy or happiness

indicators.note: dancing says the letters of the name are jiggled into a new order

explanation.surface: Joy surrounds Ron as he dances in a town in County Clare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles the name, and 'all around' wraps the joy word round it. Clare is an Irish county, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenroe is an Irish place name, here placed by the setter in County Clare, Ireland.

clue.text: During bombardment sort out required for risk-tolerant practice in 1 across

indicators.note: During says one piece sits inside the bombardment word

parts.note: shelling is bombardment with artillery

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word before it are disordered

explanation.surface: In the middle of an air raid, someone must sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles 'sort', and 'During' sets the result inside the bombardment word; 'required for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Short selling, selling borrowed stock hoping to buy it back cheaper, is a high-risk trading tactic.

clue.text: Make provision where member has died

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
someone who has died is late, so 'is late'

explanation.surface: A will specifies what happens when a member of the family dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, setting down legal provisions.

clue.text: Financial specialist in e-business backed on film

parts.note: E for electronic and CO for company, a business

indicators.note: backed says the little word is turned round

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: An expert in online business has made a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist is an expert in economics, a specialist in finance and markets.

clue.text: See 1
Invention inspired by an extraterrestrial

indicators.note: inspired by says the falsehood is breathed into, so placed inside, the word an

parts.note: a lie is an invention, something made up

explanation.surface: A creative idea comes from a visitor from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a being from another planet, a creature not of Earth.

clue.text: FT for example on this recent run

parts.note: new means recent
a sprint is a fast run

explanation.surface: The Financial Times reports on a recent race.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: newspapers like the FT are printed on this paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap paper on which newspapers, the pink FT among them, are printed.

clue.text: Ted with guitar shredding wins appreciation

indicators.note: shredding, fast guitar playing or tearing up, says the letters of Ted and guitar are torn into a new order

explanation.surface: A guitarist named Ted plays a fast solo and earns the audience's applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is thankfulness, the feeling of appreciation for what one has received.

clue.text: High-level clashes avoided where song does not make chart

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
a record that fails to get into the charts misses

explanation.surface: A song fails to reach the hit parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Air misses are near collisions between aircraft, where a crash in the sky was narrowly avoided.

clue.text: Fully and freely expressed in Dublin with Red Rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of Dublin and Red are made strange

explanation.surface: Racegoers in Dublin celebrate the famous horse Red Rum without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum was a famous British racehorse, winning the Grand National three times; here 'Rum' rearranges DUBLIN and RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbridled means unrestrained, like a horse without a bridle, so given full free expression.

clue.text: Solution in tub for women kept by vampire-slayer?

indicators.note: kept by says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a bat hater: the question mark admits this is a playful description of someone who kills vampires

explanation.surface: Buffy keeps a woman in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' is liquid in a tub, not an answer to a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathwater is the water, a liquid or solution, that fills a bathtub.

clue.text: Graduate calls bank that failed

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
rings means telephones, calls

explanation.surface: A graduate telephones a collapsed bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Barings was the old London merchant bank that collapsed in 1995 after a rogue trader's losses.

clue.text: Muslim man has unsalted fish

indicators.note: unsalted says the S, initial of salt, is taken off the word before

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
the bib, or pouting, is a small fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A man brings home some fish without salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Habib is an Arabic masculine name, meaning beloved, common among Muslim men.

clue.text: Universal beginning and end for 1 across 12

definitions.meaning: the theory of the origin of the universe
the 1986 London deregulation that led to computer trading and the end of open-outcry dealing floors

explanation.definitionFit: The cosmic explosion that began the universe, and the 1986 City deregulation that killed the dealing floor.

clue.text: Go over main points for military policeman lacking in depth

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the policeman

parts.note: a redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red caps

explanation.surface: A military policeman fails to summarise in any depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, briefly restating the main points of something.

clue.text: Comfortable with such nonsense, the end for Lansley

indicators.note: nonsense says the letters of 'such' are made a nonsense of, rearranged
the end for picks the last letter of the politician's name

explanation.surface: A politician's comfortable position is called such nonsense, and the end for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Lansley was a British Conservative health secretary. 'nonsense' makes CUSH from SUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job or position is easy and comfortable.

clue.text: Swapping of partners in group involves drugs and is severe

indicators.note: involves says the drug letter is wrapped up inside the other piece

parts.note: swinging is group partner-swapping
E is slang for ecstasy, drugs

explanation.surface: Wife-swapping in a group comes with drug-taking and is beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: SWINGEING is a British word, most often used of heavy cuts or fines.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing means severe or drastic, as in swingeing cuts.

clue.text: Fine cut for the commentator

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so this says the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with wool

explanation.surface: A commentator remarks on a fine cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is fine and translucent.

clue.text: Giving us classic couture, innovator leads as designer

indicators.note: leads says the leading, opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: An innovative fashion house gives us classic couture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gucci is the Italian fashion house and luxury label, named after the designer Guccio Gucci.

clue.text: Part for Sean Astin essential in Malevolence

indicators.note: Part says the answer is a run of letters forming part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A role for the actor Sean Astin is essential in a film called Malevolence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like an acting role, which suits the actor, but it signals a hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is ill will, a desire to harm, which is nastiness.

clue.text: Daughter to Frederick and first to Charles Lamb

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the name that follows

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote essays under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: A girl was the daughter of a man named Frederick and the first child of the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's As You Like It, Celia is the daughter of Duke Frederick.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is Duke Frederick's daughter and Rosalind's cousin in As You Like It.

clue.text: Hesitant relative is out with disreputable lawyer

parts.note: shy means hesitant or timid

indicators.note: is out says the letters of 'is' leave the relative's word

parts.note: a sister is a relative

explanation.surface: A timid relative walks out on a crooked solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous professional, especially a crooked lawyer.

clue.text: Commotion during offence hard to understand

indicators.note: during says the hard letter sits inside the offence word

parts.note: a sin is an offence
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to dig is slang for to understand

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a crime that is hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy party or a commotion and fuss.
